title: The First Thin Smile
skyStory: There it is: the first thin smile of a new moon, six percent and grinning low in the west just after sunset. Gemini is still holding the microphone and won't give it back. The moon is practising introductions for its big month ahead. Hello, I'm the moon, I do tides. Mars applauds loudly. Saturn nods once, which for Saturn is a standing ovation.

reading: A waxing moon is the universe pressing the gas pedal very gently. Things you started this week will begin to show a little green. Resist the urge to dig them up and check the roots. The [[Ace of Pentacles]] is sitting on the cabin step, shaking its head at you.

Around midday, a wave of restlessness. The Tiger paces. Instead of starting something new, go outside for ten minutes and look for the first dandelion. There will be one, bold and too early, and you'll recognise yourself in it. Tell it good job. Then go back in and finish the thing you were doing.
joel.mission: Find the first dandelion of the season and send Nancy a photo of it with a dramatic one-word caption.
joel.omen: A sliver of moon visible while it's still light out. Your effort is showing before you think it is.

reading: Something small and new is starting in your corner of the world, and you're the first to see it. Maybe it's a habit, maybe a project, maybe just a better way to fold the towels. Whatever it is, it has your fingerprints all over it.

The [[Page of Pentacles]] reversed suggests you're tempted to wait until it's perfect before showing anyone. Show it anyway, at sixty percent. Someone will add the missing piece you didn't know you needed. This is how the Wood Rat builds empires: one clever, slightly unfinished thing at a time, passed hand to hand.
nancy.mission: Show one half-finished thing to someone today and ask them for exactly one suggestion.
nancy.omen: A chalk drawing on the sidewalk, half washed away by rain. Unfinished is beautiful; keep going.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire, for a fresh start
nancy.elementWhy: new things need a little heat

together.text: Find the moon tonight just after sunset, low in the west. Whoever spots it first sends the other one word describing its shape. Not banana. Anything but banana. Saturn has banned banana. The loser makes the first move on tomorrow's plans.
